title: Doctrine of Separation of Powers & Rule of Law (Dicey's formulation)

content.overview: The doctrine of separation of powers divides state functions among legislature, executive and judiciary to prevent concentration of power. In India the separation is not rigid; the Constitution adopts checks and balances while treating separation as part of the basic structure in its essential features.
content.glance: Identify which organ's function is engaged; test whether one organ has assumed a core function of another; apply Indian checks-and-balances rather than rigid tripartite separation.
content.study: Classical separation assigns law-making, execution and adjudication to distinct organs. Indian constitutional practice is functional rather than rigid: delegated legislation, administrative adjudication and judicial review create overlaps. Courts intervene when one organ usurps the essential function of another. Separation and the rule of law are complementary limits on arbitrary power. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the Constitution. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Classical Doctrine
sections.body: Division of legislative, executive and judicial functions.

sections.heading: Indian Adaptation
sections.body: Checks and balances rather than rigid separation.

sections.heading: Essential Functions
sections.body: Core legislative, executive and judicial functions cannot be wholly usurped.

sections.heading: Overlaps
sections.body: Delegated legislation and tribunals create permitted overlaps within limits.

sections.heading: Basic Structure
sections.body: Essential separation features form part of the constitutional basic structure.

examples.title: Usurpation of judicial function
examples.body: A statute transfers a core adjudicatory function in a manner that destroys judicial independence. Essential separation features are engaged.

examples.title: Permitted overlap
examples.body: A parent Act authorises rules on details within stated policy. Delegated legislation is a permitted overlap, not a rigid-separation violation.

hypotheticals.question: Does India follow strict Montesquieu separation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Indian practice is checks and balances under a written Constitution.

hypotheticals.question: Is any overlap of functions unconstitutional?
hypotheticals.analysis: Permitted overlaps exist; the vice is usurpation of essential functions.

distinctions.title: Rigid separation vs checks and balances

misconceptions.correction: Indian practice is checks and balances under a written Constitution.

misconceptions.trap: Any overlap of functions is unconstitutional.
misconceptions.correction: Permitted overlaps exist; the vice is usurpation of essential functions.

cases.name: Ram Jawaya Kapur v State of Punjab
cases.facts: Executive action and constitutional distribution of governmental functions.
cases.issue: Whether the Indian Constitution adopts a rigid separation of powers.
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Constitution does not impose separation in absolute rigidity; functions are sufficiently differentiated.
cases.holding: Functional separation rather than strict Montesquieuan separation recognised.
cases.relevance: Principal Indian authority on functional separation.

cases.name: Asif Hameed v State of Jammu and Kashmir
cases.facts: Limits of judicial intervention in matters allocated to other organs.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Each constitutional organ must operate within its assigned sphere.

cases.name: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
cases.issue: Whether separation of powers forms part of the constitutional structure.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Checks and balances and separation of powers are components of the basic structure.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a separation-of-powers problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify organs and functions. II. Test usurpation of essential function. III. Apply Indian checks-and-balances. IV. Note basic-structure implications if any.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Organs identified; function alleged to be usurped; Indian standard; precise relief.
